newsitem.title: USA: U.S. weekly cash lumber review - May 9.
newsitem.headline: U.S. weekly cash lumber review - May 9.

text.p: Random Lengths Gross List Cash Lumber Prices Quotes:
(2x4 Std&Btr) WEEKLY MIDWEEK PREV WK YR AGO

COMMENT - A pickup in the trading pace Thursday was not enough to overcome earlier sluggishness, and most prices finished lower. Most producers waited until Wednesday to aggressively seek business, said the Random Lengths cash lumber report for the week ended Friday.

However, when some openly solicited orders and showed flexibility in their places, wholesalers covered shorts and found plenty of back-to-back business. Dealers were skittish about stocking up at current prices, even as jobsite activity picked up seasonally.
Concerns that downside risk outweighs the upside potential kept some buyers on the sidelines.
Some producers tried to ride out the early-week lull and still-comfortable order files enabled many to hang tough. However, others with wood hitting the floor lowered quotes and opened to counters.

After some mills firmed prices Thursday, many dealers turned back to booking truckloads from distribution yards and reloads. A strong upward move in the soon-to-close May futures contract encouraged traders looking for reasons to be bullish' however, futures prices ended Thursday close to par with cash prices.

Southern Pine, the dimension market's leader in recent weeks, was not immune to the rollbacks; a few items were sharply discounted to unload buildups. Availability of trucks was a growing problem across much of the South as the produce season is well under way.

Trading in western species was spotty, and most prices moved down a notch. Railcar shortages frustrated some producers in the Northwest. Green Fir was more available due to a slowdown in oversupplied export markets. British Columbia labor talks heated up, catching the attention of some traders.
Canadian export quota used as of about May 1 was 9.6 percent.
